value: Opportunity Colleges and Universities – Higher Access, Higher Earnings
description: Carnegie's flagship SAEC bucket: institutions whose Pell-receiving undergraduate share is at or above the overall sector benchmark AND whose 10-year-after-entry earnings outcomes are at or above the expected benchmark for their student population. Read as "high access AND high outcomes" — institutions delivering social mobility at scale.
Above-benchmark Pell share and above-benchmark earnings outcomes, but distinct from the flagship Opportunity Colleges tier.
Above-benchmark Pell share with mid-range earnings outcomes for the institution's student population.
Above-benchmark Pell share with below-benchmark earnings outcomes. Often institutions serving lower-income students whose outcomes do not yet exceed expectation.

Below-benchmark Pell share with above-benchmark earnings outcomes. The classic "selective high-income with strong outcomes" profile — Holy Cross sits here, along with most selective LACs and many national universities.
Below-benchmark Pell share with mid-range earnings outcomes.
Below-benchmark on both axes. Often small specialty institutions or schools where degree-level outcomes are limited.

Excluded from the SAEC framework. Typically includes service academies, special-focus institutions, very small institutions, and others where the Pell and earnings benchmarks don't apply meaningfully.

value: Research 1: Very High Spending and Doctorate Production
description: R1: highest tier of doctoral universities by combined research spending and PhDs awarded. The ~140 most research-intensive institutions in the US.

value: Research 2: High Spending and Doctorate Production
description: R2: doctoral universities with high research activity, below the R1 threshold.
Institutions with measurable research activity that don't meet the R1/R2 doctoral thresholds. Often master's institutions or smaller research-active colleges.
No formal research classification. Includes most baccalaureate colleges and institutions whose research activity is below Carnegie's threshold.
More than 50% of full-time undergraduates live on campus.
75% or more of full-time undergraduates live on campus. The most residential category. (Note: "residental" is spelled this way in the source Carnegie data.)
Significant on-campus housing, but a smaller share than the Residential tiers.
Fewer than 25% of full-time undergraduates live on campus. Most students commute.
Few on-campus residents, but a primarily full-time student body.
Few on-campus residents and a primarily part-time student body. Common for working-adult-focused institutions.
Most enrollment is via online courses; minimal on-campus presence.
Substantial mix of online and on-campus students.
Limited or no undergraduate population; institution is centered on graduate education.
Public 4-year institutions (IPEDS SECTOR = 1). Includes state universities and state college systems.
Private nonprofit 4-year institutions (IPEDS SECTOR = 2). Excludes for-profit institutions, which are excluded from the project universe entirely.
Institutions formally affiliated with the Roman Catholic Church (per IPEDS IC2023 RELAFFIL = 30).

Institutions affiliated with denominationally-specific Protestant traditions (Lutheran, Methodist, Presbyterian, Baptist, and so on). See R/schools_pipeline.R for the full denomination-to-tradition mapping.
Eastern Orthodox, Latter-day Saints, and nondenominational / ecumenical / multi-denominational Christian institutions.
Jewish-affiliated institutions.
Muslim, Buddhist, Unitarian Universalist, and other religious traditions not captured by the above categories.
